situation:
You are the controller at STONEHOLLOW DATA CENTERS, a family-owned data center operator that rents secure server space to hospitals, banks and software firms. The president (judge) is the third generation of the family to run the business, and has asked you to recommend how the company should pay to replace the failing cooling plant in its original building.

The chillers in that building are twenty-two years old and nearly fully depreciated. Repair spending has climbed every year, and the last two failures dropped the building below the uptime the company reports to its clients each month. The insurer will not renew outage coverage there unless the chillers are replaced this year. A new plant would cost more than the company has on hand and would be carried as a long-term asset for fifteen years.

The president (judge) will not borrow against the family's property, so the money has to come from clients, and the two ways of raising it land on two different groups of them. One course of action is to end the frozen rates held for the fifteen oldest clients in the original building, several of them customers for thirty years. Those rates were a promise the president's (judge) grandfather made, and ending them would cost the company the trust of the clients its name was built on; the sales team expects at least three of them to leave.

The other course of action is to raise every client's rate by the same small amount, including the clients in the newer building, who sit on cooling installed four years ago and have never lost a minute of service. They would be paying for equipment they will never use, and the company competes for their renewals against operators that can hold their prices flat.

The president (judge) wants a recommendation on which course of action to take, how the company should measure whether it worked once it is in place, and what the finance staff owes each client in the way of explanation. The president (judge) will greet you, ask to hear your ideas, and will thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the president (judge) of STONEHOLLOW DATA CENTERS. Business background is the same as the situation above.

You are the third generation of the family to run this business, and the cooling plant in the original building has to be replaced this year whether or not the money is comfortable to raise. You want to hear which course of action the controller recommends — ending the frozen rates for the fifteen oldest clients, or raising every client's rate by the same small amount — and exactly how the recommendation would be carried out.

During the presentation you will ask the following questions:
